4.speaker: Lucian Galade
4.text: “Ms. Agnoc. Don't forget whom you are speaking with.”

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: Lucian and I arrived at the Ministry of Economy.

10.speaker: Narrator
10.text: Assistants took our coats and showed us into the meeting room where Symon, Edith, Gus and Mikail were waiting.

11.speaker: Narrator
11.text: As soon as I entered, their chatter stopped and they stood up. After a few pleasantries, everyone but Symon took their seats.

12.speaker: Narrator
12.text: He opened his briefcase, produced a folder and proceeded to go over some of the documents.

13.speaker: Symon Holl
13.text: “Greetings, everyone. Welcome to the Ministry of Economy.”

15.speaker: Symon Holl
15.text: “We are here today to discuss our economic move towards nationalization.”

16.speaker: Symon Holl
16.text: “We are of course here today to discuss our economic shift towards privatization.”

18.speaker: Narrator
18.text: Both Mikail and Edith had their arms crossed and frowns on their faces. They were listening intently.

19.speaker: Symon Holl
19.text: “Before you arrived, certain individuals in this room were voicing their opinion against a nationalization plan.”

20.speaker: Symon Holl
20.text: “But as I understand it, your decision has already been made."

23.speaker: Player
23.text: “Yes. And you will respect my decision whether you like it or not.”

25.speaker: Edith Agnoc
25.text: “I am very much against a nationalization plan.”

29.speaker: Narrator
29.text: One look from Symon stopped her. Both she and Mikail were restless in their seats.

30.speaker: Player
30.text: “This is for the good of our country.”

32.speaker: Edith Agnoc
32.text: “Nationalization could provide an improvement in terms of our economic development in the next year or two."

33.speaker: Edith Agnoc
33.text: “But in the long term, you are losing people's trust. Without trust, there can be little trade. Especially if the government excessively nationalizes entire industries. Besides, it will cost us a proportional amount of government budget to nationalize.”

34.speaker: Player
34.text: “And you personally won't be able to profit. Isn't that right, Ms. Agnoc?”

36.speaker: Player
36.text: “Are you saying that the state of Sordland is untrustworthy?”

37.speaker: Player
37.text: “I've heard enough. You will accept my decision regardless.”

38.speaker: Edith Agnoc
38.text: “No. Of course it is trustworthy. That is not my point.”

40.speaker: Lucian Galade
40.text: “Let's not get ahead of ourselves, shall we?”

43.speaker: Symon Holl
43.text: “Let's move on to how we can go about implementing a nationalization plan.”

46.speaker: Narrator
46.text: He handed me and everyone else in the room two neat stacks of documents.

49.speaker: Symon Holl
49.text: “As you can see on the document, the first corporation up for discussion is Heart of Sordland.”

50.speaker: Symon Holl
50.text: “Led by fledgling CEO Marcel Koronti, HOS has recently observed a boost in their revenue. They control many media organisations across Sordland.”

51.speaker: Symon Holl
51.text: “It is possible to see their imprint everywhere from newspaper stands to convenience stores. In fact, they own more than half of the media products in the country.”

52.speaker: Symon Holl
52.text: “We all know how much of an effect media has on politics.”

53.speaker: Symon Holl
53.text: “I must add that I myself am against fully nationalizing any of these companies in principle.”

55.speaker: Symon Holl
55.text: “That is the reason I think if we are to nationalize any corporation, HOS should be our target.”

56.speaker: Symon Holl
56.text: “However, we could partially move the ownership of HOS to the state, gaining access to their income to help end the recession and provide for our citizens.”

57.speaker: Lucian Galade
57.text: “I am inclined to agree with you from a political perspective. However...”

58.speaker: Lucian Galade
58.text: “If we are going to nationalize HOS, I think we should go all the way and fully move its ownership to the state.”

70.speaker: Symon Holl
70.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn07_EnT_HOS_Full"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn07_EnT_HOS_Majority"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn07_EnT_HOS_Minority"] == true) == false

71.speaker: Player
71.text: “What would the effects be if we fully nationalize Heart of Sordland?”

72.speaker: Player
72.text: “What if we just assume minority ownership of HOS?”

74.speaker: Player
74.text: “I already know what to do. Let's move on to our next option.”
74.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn07_EnT_HOS_Full"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn07_EnT_HOS_Majority"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn07_EnT_HOS_Minority"] == true) == false

75.speaker: Player
75.text: “Let's move on to our next option.”

78.speaker: Edith Agnoc
78.text: “They'd be disastrous, is what they would be."

79.speaker: Edith Agnoc
79.text: “Thousands of assets belonging to Marcel Koronti would now belong to the state. This would scare off many investors and most likely stop new money from coming in.”

80.speaker: Mikail Aven
80.text: “I am against fully nationalizing any company."

81.speaker: Mikail Aven
81.text: “But if you insist on nationalizing something regardless, I would pick HOS.”

84.speaker: Mikail Aven
84.text: “Marcel Koronti is growing too powerful too fast."

85.speaker: Mikail Aven
85.text: “The next thing you know, he could even have control over the state newspapers!”

87.speaker: Lucian Galade
87.text: “At first glance, a minority share might make sense. However, I don't think it's a good idea.”

88.speaker: Lucian Galade
88.text: “It would only serve to make Koronti angry at the state while retaining enough power to damage us.”

89.speaker: Symon Holl
89.text: “In the case of HOS, I do agree.”

90.speaker: Symon Holl
90.text: “I believe this is the way to go.”

91.speaker: Symon Holl
91.text: “We would have board control over HOS and supplementary funds for government projects.”

92.speaker: Lucian Galade
92.text: “Theoretically. But we would still be making an enemy out of Marcel Koronti. He wouldn't be as powerful, of course, but I believe it's safer to move him off the chess board entirely."

95.speaker: Symon Holl
95.text: “It is the largest fully private corporation among the Big Four and a dominant force in steel manufacturing for many years.”

96.speaker: Symon Holl
96.text: “It is led by current CEO and Lotherberg spokesman Walter Tusk. I believe all of us in the room are familiar with him in one way or another.”

97.speaker: Symon Holl
97.text: “What can I say? They have been widely successful since their founding. They have achieved renown not only in Sordland, but worldwide.”

98.speaker: Symon Holl
98.text: “I believe we shouldn't attempt to break something that is already working. I am against the nationalization of Bergia Steel in any capacity.”

99.speaker: Mikail Aven
99.text: “Not to mention any amount of nationalization would be disastrous for both Bergia Steel and Sordland.”

100.speaker: Mikail Aven
100.text: “Much of our steel trade is reliant on their manufacturing capabilities. Any sudden change there would be like throwing a screwdriver in a working engine.”

101.speaker: Edith Agnoc
101.text: “No matter what, we should refrain from nationalizing them. It could result in an economic crisis.”

102.speaker: Lucian Galade
102.text: “I don't have so strong of an opinion. But I will say that nationalizing both Bergia Steel and HOS would be quite unwise."

106.speaker: Player
106.text: “What would the effects be if we fully nationalize Bergia Steel?”

107.speaker: Player
107.text: “What are your thoughts on a minority share?”

111.speaker: Player
111.text: “I have already decided on what we need to do.”
111.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn07_EnT_BergiaSteel_Full"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn07_EnT_BergiaSteel_Majority"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn07_EnT_BergiaSteel_Minority"] == true) == false

112.speaker: Player
112.text: “What would be the outcome of taking a majority share?”

113.speaker: Player
113.text: “I am ready to make a decision.”

119.speaker: Symon Holl
119.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn07_EnT_BergiaSteel_Full"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn07_EnT_BergiaSteel_Majority"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn07_EnT_BergiaSteel_Minority"] == true) == false

125.speaker: Mikail Aven
125.text: “They are quite literally the backbone of Sordland's private economy.”

126.speaker: Mikail Aven
126.text: “If you do this, you will anger many powerful people. Trust me, you don't want that.”

129.speaker: Player
129.text: “I understand the predicament, but it is necessary.”

130.speaker: Player
130.text: “Let them come. I am not afraid.”

131.speaker: Player
131.text: “You are right. I don't want more enemies.”

134.speaker: Edith Agnoc
134.text: “You can simply not do it and you will achieve peace.”

137.speaker: Symon Holl
137.text: “As I mentioned, I am against making changes to Bergia Steel's ownership.”

138.speaker: Symon Holl
138.text: “We should leave the company as it is.”

139.speaker: Lucian Galade
139.text: “I tend to agree. But only because HOS is the weaker of the two and it is less risky to deal with them as opposed to a giant like Bergia Steel.”

141.speaker: Symon Holl
141.text: “This is of course a better option than full nationalization. But that doesn't mean you would not face adversity.”

142.speaker: Symon Holl
142.text: “A majority share means Bergia Steel would experience a massive drop in status.”

143.speaker: Symon Holl
143.text: “This would surely anger a man like Walter Tusk.”

144.speaker: Symon Holl
144.text: “And if I may make an understatement, he is not a forgiving man.”

145.speaker: Player
145.text: “No need to be afraid. If push comes to shove, I will handle it.”

146.speaker: Player
146.text: “He is scary for sure. I would hate to make an enemy out of him.”

147.speaker: Symon Holl
147.text: “It's the administration I'm worried about. Not only you."

148.speaker: Player
148.text: “If that day comes, Walter Tusk will learn Anton Rayne is *also* not a forgiving man.”

150.speaker: Lucian Galade
150.text: “He seems to hold everyone in his pocket.”

155.speaker: Symon Holl
155.text: “Let's go over the document once again then.”

156.speaker: Narrator
156.text: I read all of Symon's documents once more, then flipped to the last page.

157.speaker: Narrator
157.text: It was time to make some decisions.

161.speaker: Symon Holl
161.text: “Especially since we were initially going down the path of a market economy.”

163.speaker: Symon Holl
163.text: “Before you arrived, Mikail and Edith were expressing their delight at your decision to go down this path."

165.speaker: Edith Agnoc
165.text: “This was certainly the right decision. It will boost our economy by providing the government much-needed funds right now.”

169.speaker: Mikail Aven
169.text: “I'm glad we're staying firmly on the path to a market economy.”

170.speaker: Mikail Aven
170.text: “I know a market economy wasn't part of your original plans, but I'm happy you've seen the light."

171.speaker: Edith Agnoc
171.text: “We can then use these funds to increase development for the future. It's a win-win situation for sure.”

172.speaker: Player
172.text: “You are saying this only because you will have a stake in it.”

173.speaker: Player
173.text: “I am glad we are on the same page.”

176.speaker: Edith Agnoc
176.text: “Of course not! I am saying this because all along I knew you would make the right choice for Sordland.”

178.speaker: Edith Agnoc
178.text: “I have to give credit when it's due.”

179.speaker: Symon Holl
179.text: “Let's move on to how we can go about implementing a privatization plan.”

180.speaker: Narrator
180.text: Symon handed me and everyone else in the room two neat stacks of documents.

183.speaker: Symon Holl
183.text: “As you can see on the document, the first company up for discussion is the Sordish State Corporation.”

184.speaker: Symon Holl
184.text: “The Sordish State Corporation, or SSC for short, has been around for over half a century. Most recently they have been handling a wide range of state construction projects.”

185.speaker: Symon Holl
185.text: “In their portfolio they have government buildings, various infrastructure projects, state libraries, embassies. Basically anything government-related.”

186.speaker: Symon Holl
186.text: “Privatizing a company like this would certainly increase the government's budget. That, of course, would result in lots of opportunities for us to provide for our citizens.”

187.speaker: Lucian Galade
187.text: “The funds could also be used to boost our popularity. Especially with the elections approaching.”

188.speaker: Lucian Galade
188.text: “Not to mention the various other areas in which we can and should spend money."

190.speaker: Lucian Galade
190.text: “The conservative majority of the USP would not like this decision. At all. For them, these state companies are part and parcel of Sordish identity.”

191.speaker: Lucian Galade
191.text: “If we privatize these companies entirely and sell too many shares in them, it will have consequences for us in the Assembly.”

196.speaker: Player
196.text: “What would the effects be if we fully privatize the Sordish State Corporation?”

197.speaker: Player
197.text: “What if we sell a minority share of SSC?”

200.speaker: Symon Holl
200.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn07_EnT_SSC_Full"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn07_EnT_SSC_Majority"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn07_EnT_SSC_Minority"] == true) == false

212.speaker: Player
212.text: “I already know what to do. Let's move on to the next option.”
212.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn07_EnT_SSC_Full"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn07_EnT_SSC_Majority"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn07_EnT_SSC_Minority"] == true) == false

213.speaker: Player
213.text: “Let's move on to the next option.”

216.speaker: Symon Holl
216.text: “We would gain tremendous amounts of money for the government.”

217.speaker: Symon Holl
217.text: “We can invest that money in future government projects which would popularise our administration, increasing the chances for our re-election.”

218.speaker: Lucian Galade
218.text: “That popularity might not make up for losing the lion's share of the conservative vote.”

219.speaker: Lucian Galade
219.text: “Conservatives comprise the majority of the Assembly. If we hurt their national pride, they'll turn on us.”

220.speaker: Lucian Galade
220.text: “I am against full privatization. We shouldn't make enemies at this stage.”

221.speaker: Edith Agnoc
221.text: “It would be better than nothing, but why stop there?"

222.speaker: Edith Agnoc
222.text: “A minority stake won't help our government as much.”

224.speaker: Lucian Galade
224.text: “On the other hand, a minority share would create less friction. This would be my preference.”

225.speaker: Mikail Aven
225.text: “This is certainly a very good option.”

226.speaker: Mikail Aven
226.text: “The state would keep some of SSC's operations under control, and the government would have lots of gains.”

227.speaker: Symon Holl
227.text: “I am leaning towards this option myself.”

228.speaker: Symon Holl
228.text: “Retaining control while increasing our budget -- I don't see a downside.”

230.speaker: Symon Holl
230.text: “It is one of the largest mining corporations in Eastern Merkopa, let alone Sordland.”

231.speaker: Symon Holl
231.text: “They call themselves the leaders of the world in coal. They certainly have enough evidence to back that up.”

232.speaker: Symon Holl
232.text: “Perhaps they are not as large as SSC, but we still have a lot to gain if Nedam Mining Group is privatised.”

233.speaker: Symon Holl
233.text: “I fully support privatization of this company to any extent.”

234.speaker: Symon Holl
234.text: “Certainly a good option to gain enough capital to end the recession once and for all.”

235.speaker: Edith Agnoc
235.text: “I have contacts in Nedam. It is one of the most valuable corporations of the last decade.”

236.speaker: Mikail Aven
236.text: “I can vouch for that. I have personal experience with the company myself. It would be a great addition to any portfolio.”

240.speaker: Player
240.text: “What would the effects be if we fully privatize Nedam Mining Group?”

241.speaker: Player
241.text: “What are your thoughts on selling a minority share?”

250.speaker: Player
250.text: “I am ready to make a decision.”

256.speaker: Symon Holl
256.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn07_EnT_Nedam_Full"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn07_EnT_Nedam_Majority"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn07_EnT_Nedam_Minority"] == true) == false

257.speaker: Player
257.text: “I have already decided what we need to do.”
257.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn07_EnT_Nedam_Full"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn07_EnT_Nedam_Majority"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn07_EnT_Nedam_Minority"] == true) == false

259.speaker: Symon Holl
259.text: “Let's go over the document once again then.”

261.speaker: Mikail Aven
261.text: “It would be a very profitable sell.”

262.speaker: Edith Agnoc
262.text: “I know many people who would kill to have a portion of that company.”

263.speaker: Symon Holl
263.text: “I do think this is a good option.”

264.speaker: Symon Holl
264.text: “We could simply fully privatize Nedam along with SSC to bring in a large influx of money to the government.”

266.speaker: Lucian Galade
266.text: “I hate to repeat myself, but fully privatizing one state-owned company -- let alone two -- will anger our conservative voter base.”

267.speaker: Lucian Galade
267.text: “All the budget in the world won't matter if you aren't re-elected.”

268.speaker: Lucian Galade
268.text: “Coupled with a minority share of SSC, that is the way to go.”

269.speaker: Symon Holl
269.text: “It would, however, be a lost opportunity. I think we should sell a majority share instead.”

270.speaker: Edith Agnoc
270.text: “Definitely not a bad idea at all.”

271.speaker: Symon Holl
271.text: “My preference is selling a majority share of both SSC and Nedam.”

272.speaker: Symon Holl
272.text: “It would give us the most value. I think we should go with this choice.”

273.speaker: Lucian Galade
273.text: “This might still generate a backlash from the Assembly and the general public."

274.speaker: Lucian Galade
274.text: “We should go for a minority share instead.”

275.speaker: Narrator
275.text: I read all of Symon's documents once more, then flipped to the last page.

276.speaker: Narrator
276.text: It was time to make some decisions.
